newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish doctors plan pay strike from Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish doctors plan pay strike from Tuesday.

text.p: A medical trade union affiliating one-third of Poland's 100,000 physicians has announced an indefinite pay strike, PAP new agency said on Monday.
"On Tuesday the All-Poland Medical Doctors' Union (OZZL) is starting an open-ended doctors' strike," PAP quoted its leader Krzysztof Bukiel as saying.
Some 600 of the country's 815 hospitals and about one-half of its out-patient clinics are expected to take part in the action, he told a news conference.
Routine operations, medical tests and other health services will not be available for the duration of the protest, and only life-threatening cases will be treated.

The strikers' are demanding a separate collective wage deal for doctors which would increase their monthly salaries to about 3,000 zlotys (more than $1,000) -- three times the average industrial wage.
They also want more state funding for the health service's deteriorating infrastructure.
"The strike will be interrupted the moment the government agrees to two-way talks only with doctors, not with the entire health service," Bukiel said.
A Health Ministry spokesman Wojciech Rudnicki said that under existing rules there was no possibility of separate negotations with doctors without the consent of other health workers.
Maternity and children's hospitals, cancer wards and psychiatric facilities will be exempted from the action.
